simple.meaning: חָטַב (châṭab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to chop or carve wood.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 9 times in Deuteronomy, Joshua, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Jeremiah, and 1 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 19:5. The surrounding contexts include altar, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָטַב (H2404) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָטַב (châṭab) / H2404 is traced through Deuteronomy 19:5, Deuteronomy 29:10, Joshua 9:21, Joshua 9:23 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to chop wood and his hand swings the ax to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle and hits his neighbor so that he dies—he shall flee to one of these cities and live.

timeline.evidenceText: as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to chop wood and his hand swings the ax to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle and hits his neighbor so that he dies—he shall flee to one of these cities and live.
All of you stand today in the presence of Yahweh your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, even all the men of Israel,
The princes said to them, “Let them live.” So they became wood cutters and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the princes had spoken to them.
Now therefore you are cursed, and some of you will never fail to be slaves, both wood cutters and drawers of water for the house of my God.”
That day Joshua made them wood cutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for Yahweh’s altar to this day, in the place which he should choose.
even to prepare me timber in abundance; for the house which I am about to build will be great and wonderful.
Then our sons will be like well-nurtured plants,
Its sound will go like the serpent;

so that they will take no wood out of the field, and not cut down any out of the forests; for they will make fires with the weapons. They will plunder those who plundered them, and rob those who robbed them,” says the Lord Yahweh.

definitions.full: H2404. chatab I. [ חָטַב ] verb cut or gather wood , usually firewood (Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic firewood , collect firewood (see Wetzst in De Psa 144:12 ); Ethiopic cut (or gather) firewood ) — Qal Imperfect יַחְטְבוּ Ezek 39:10 ; Infinitive לַחְטֹב Deut 19:5 ; Participle חֹטֵב 29:10 ; plural חֹטְבִים 2Chr 2:9 ; construct חֹטְבֵי Josh 9:21 3 t.; passive plural feminine חֲטֻבוֺת Prov 7:16 — cut or gather wood, followed by accusative Deut 19:5 ; 29:10 (|| מים שׁאב ); compare Ezek 39:10 מןהֿיערים (object in preceding clause); 2Chr 2:9 (|| הָעֵצִים כֹּרְתֵי ); Participle construct ׳ח עצים Jer 46:22 , and (|| מַיִם שֹׁאֲבֵי ) Josh 9:21 , 23 , 27 . Pu`al Participle מְחֻטָּבוֺת Psa 144:12 meaning dubious; perhaps hewn (so, in substance, Thes MV SS Ew Che Bae; see however II. חטב ), of corner-pillars ( זָוִיּוֺת see זָוִית above), simile of beautiful, stately daughters. II. חטב (√of following; compare Arabic be of the colour , i.e. turbid, dusky, mixed with yellowish red , etc.; Aramaic Participle variegated ᵑ6 2Sam 13:19 ).
